title: Ge/ZnS Two-Cavity Fabry-Perot Dual-Bandpass Filter with 20 Layers
scientific_hypothesis: A two-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter using Ge (high-index) and ZnS (low-index) quarter-wave stacks on CaF2 substrate can achieve simultaneous transmission peaks at 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm with strong blocking in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm stopbands within 20 layers.
design_principle: Start with alternating quarter-wave layers at center wavelengths of each passband, form two coupled Fabry-Perot cavities separated by Bragg reflectors, then computationally optimize all layer thicknesses to shape dual passbands while maintaining stopband rejection. Ge/ZnS pair provides high index contrast (~4.0/2.3) for mid-IR with low absorption.
proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | [Ge/ZnS]_5 | Ge cavity1 | [ZnS/Ge]_3 | ZnS cavity2 | [Ge/ZnS]_5 | Air incident. Total finite layers: 20 (10 Ge + 10 ZnS).
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm stopband
minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm stopband
manufacturing_considerations: Ge and ZnS are standard mid-IR coating materials
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for layered media
expected_advantages: High index contrast enables fewer layers for given blocking
Ge/ZnS pair verified for 3-5 μm mid-IR range
Two-cavity design allows dual passband shaping
known_risks: Ge absorption may increase beyond 5 μm
Stress mismatch between Ge and ZnS
Fabrication tolerance sensitivity for narrow bands
execution_request_english: Design and optimize a 20-layer dielectric multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate for dual-bandpass transmission. Layer stack: CaF2 | Layer1(Ge) | Layer2(ZnS) | Layer3(Ge) | Layer4(ZnS) | Layer5(Ge) | Layer6(ZnS) | Layer7(Ge) | Layer8(ZnS) | Layer9(Ge) | Layer10(ZnS) | Layer11(Ge) | Layer12(ZnS) | Layer13(Ge) | Layer14(ZnS) | Layer15(Ge) | Layer16(ZnS) | Layer17(Ge) | Layer18(ZnS) | Layer19(Ge) | Layer20(ZnS) | Air. Optimize all 20 layer thicknesses in range 100-2000 nm. Wavelength range: 3600-5200 nm with dense sampling. Incident medium: Air at 0 degrees. Substrate: CaF2. Target: maximize transmittance in 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm bands, minimize transmittance in 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm bands. Use multi-objective optimization with weighted spectral averaging. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
revision_reason: Previous route failed compilation due to material identifier truncation ('si' instead of 'sio2'). This route uses explicit valid material names (Ge, ZnS, CaF2) and fixes the layer specification to be TMM-compiler compatible. Topology changed from periodic stack to 2-cavity Fabry-Perot based on evidence for dual-bandpass applications.
